Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.300 of 2017, under Section 498A, 304 IPC,
P.S. Dewa, District Barabanki.
3.

In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the son of the applicant around 8 to 9 years ago and subsequently, the entire matrimonial family used to harass her and burned her to death on 06.07.2017.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argues that the son of the applicant was tried for the offence alongwith the applicant and his trial concluded in the conviction under Section 304 Part II of the IPC vide judgment dated 30.03.2022.
In terms of the said judgment, he was awarded a sentence of seven years which was reduced in appeal by this Court vide order dated 16.03.2023 passed in Criminal Appeal No.776 of 2023.

It is argued that the applicant has a separate living, as such, she was not aware and never received any summons for trial and subsequently, the applicant had approached this Court by filing an Application U/S 482 No.12329 of 2023 which was disposed off by this Court vide order dated 18.12.2023 with the liberty to decide the bail application expeditiously in accordance with law.
It is argued that subsequently on surrender, the applicant was apprehended and is in custody since 06.01.2024.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant also places reliance on the statement of PW 1 recorded before the trial Court which led to the conviction order dated 30.03.2022 wherein allegations were levelled against the son of the applicant and nothing was stated against the applicant.
It is, thus, argued that the applicant who is a lady and aged about 70 years may be enlarged on bail.

6. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application by arguing that the applicant did not co-operate with the trial and continued to avoid the trial proceedings for almost five years without there being any explanation.

It is further argued that once the trial Court has convicted one of the co-accused,
there has to be a presumption that the applicant would also be convicted similarly, as such, the bail application should be rejected.

7. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, on prima-facie perusal of the statement of PW 1 during trial, which resulted into conviction order dated 30.03.2022 in respect of the son of the applicant, allegations were levelled against the son of the applicant and not against the applicant;
and apart from the said, there is a specific assertion that the applicant was having a separate living.
Considering the said facts coupled with the fact that the applicant is aged about 70 years and is a lady, she is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Smt. Maya Devi be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on her furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which she is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
